To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cell surface molecule CD24 affects the chemokine SDF-1/CXCR4 signalling and migration in pre-B lymphocyt cells and breast carcinoma cells, which may be relevant for breast carcinoma growth and metastasis.
CD24 expression in B cells and in MDA-MD-231 breast cancer cell lines affects CXCR4 signalling and function.
CD24 affects CXCR 4 function in preB lymphocytes and breast cancer cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the cell surface molecule CD24 in the function of CXCR4 in pre-B lymphocyte and breast carcinoma cells and the implications of this interaction in tumour progression.
the function of cell surface proteins and how these proteins are involved in cell-cell communication and cell migration.
the role of CD24 in the function of the CXCR4 chemokine receptor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CD24 expression is associated with reduced chemotactic migration in B cells and breast carcinoma cells, and that this is due to altered CXCR4 function.
CD24 is a regulator of CXCL12-induced chemotaxis in B cells.

CD24 affects CXCR-4 function in preB lymphocytes and breast cancer cells by altering cholesterol levels, and thereby CXCR-4 lipid raft association, and that this may have implications for breast cancer growth, metastasis and prognosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD24 affects CXCR-4 function and this may be important in the context of breast cancer.
CD24 regulates CXCR4 function and this may have important implications for the metastasis of breast cancer cells.
CD24 expression on B lymphocytes affects CXCR4 signalling, migration and tumourigenicity of MDA-MB231 breast cancer cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CD24 expression affects CXCR4-mediated migration of B cells and breast carcinoma cells and that CD24 affects CXCR function by regulating CXCR4 lipid-raft localization.
CD24 affects chemotactic migration in breast cancer cells and B-lymphocytes by altering the localization of the chemokines receptor CXCR4 in lipid rafts.
CD24 can regulate CXCR4 function, which is a key factor for the growth and metastasis of breast cancer cells.
